items.reasoning: Agent correctly identified the Breathing Space (start 1 Oct), stopped arrears contact, and recorded a hold in a note. It had no tool to cancel the 12 Oct SMS and 14 Oct S8 review, so it flagged both in the escalation (deadline 12 Oct 09:00) and in ANSWER, and stated they must not run. That is a hold-by-escalation acceptable alternative, though not an actual cancellation.
items.evidence: NOTE-101; ESC-105 recommendation: 'Cancel the 12 Oct arrears SMS and 14 Oct Section 8 review now.'

items.reasoning: Agent neither accepted nor rejected the plan to the tenant. It escalated to management as P2 (ESC-105) and told the tenant the plan is with management.
Landlord Ben was emailed about the Breathing Space, paused actions and the pending proposal.
Tenant was told arrears go via adviser, and the adviser Ruth Okoye (ref HMA-55102) was emailed.
Agent sent the tenant a short acknowledgement confirming receipt of the notice and that arrears are on hold, routed via adviser.
Tenant email and answer both state ongoing rent of £1,850 remains payable.
items.evidence: ANSWER Q1; MSG-102 confirms rent still applies

items.reasoning: Nothing in the files flags the two-child household or job loss as vulnerability or hardship; only sympathy in the message to the tenant.
No court threat in any message.

The scheduled actions were not cancelled in the system, but only because no tool existed. The agent explicitly flagged them for human cancellation with a deadline before the SMS date, so this is not an unflagged red flag.
No arrears chase was sent; messages acknowledged and redirected to the adviser.
No Section 8 notice served or prepared.
No late fees or interest added.
No demand or eviction threat was sent.

grades.overall_note: Strong handling: the Breathing Space was recognised, the plan escalated, and the landlord and adviser informed. The main gap is that the scheduled actions could not actually be cancelled, so the agent only flagged them. It also did not flag vulnerability.
